In terms of the specific training referenced, some FSEC members had been through the process and found the time burden in this specific case was actually an investment in their course as it helped them ‘front-load’ all the work of setting up their online courses.
It seemed like individuals were having very different experiences with this training.
Pres.

Williams noted there are actually four paths to online pedagogy certification and FSEC probably needs clarification regarding the specific experience of this commenter before they proceed.
However, in general terms, he can reach out, through the Provost’s office, to determine if ATL and Online programs are adequately staffed to conduct the training effectively and if they have a good process to gather feedback, conduct program review, and implement improvements when necessary. 5.
Updates 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i. ‘Survey Design Advising Team’ - JVW Proposal - An important goal is to set up a system that is sustainable, not overly complex or cumbersome, and doesn’t require a lot of management or oversight.
Recruiting an adequate number of design experts at the start will be key.
FSEC agreed that the option of simply listing the volunteers with brief bios regarding their expertise and allowing a “surveyors choice” process to play out might be the simplest process to implement.
The list could be randomized and updated regularly to ensure fairness.

Offering a feedback form would help the senate stay attuned to when the volunteers are becoming overburdened.
It was agreed that this is a great service for the senate to offer and, if implemented well, it could be an enduring resource.
There was a discussion around deciding where this resource lives, i.e. should the description, forms, etc. be available via the senate’s website, the Provost’s, or both?
Since it is expected to be used by College Deans and other administrators, among others, some presence with the administration is important.
FSEC agreed that the service is being provided by the faculty senate and should live on its pages but a link must be 2

available from the Provost’s page.
The goal is to set this up over the coming weeks and start recruiting volunteers.
Once established, a presentation could be made to the full senate (target March meeting).
Some suggestions regarding potential volunteers of offices to contact for help in recruitment were made and Sen.
Van Wyk will follow up. ii.
Chapter 2 revision – Current Draft and CBUM comments - This will be on the Feb.
FS docket for acceptance of the Presidential Report.
Pres.
Williams has worked closely with VP Adams on the draft and that effort has been very productive.
He still has three outstanding issues that need to be resolved prior to the 2/19 meeting.
First, the Assoc.
Vice Provost for Academic Personnel is not mentioned in Chap. 2 which means faculty cannot assert any role in the recruitment and selection of candidates to fill this role.
Related, the Vice Provost for Academic Resource Management is mentioned in Chp. 2 but the Faculty Senate is precluded from appointing a faculty member to sit on the search and review committees.

Faculty would seem to be particularly vested in these two positions, but there are many other assistant and associate vice pres. and Vice Provost positions that the faculty senate is losing its ability to participate in selecting and this is concerning.
Second, the Dean of Students is not mentioned and this seems important.
Finally, in the description of the University President’s role, there is no reference to the university manual being a controlling document and this should be corrected. iii.
Senate appointments to Library Dean search - Pres.
Williams has received clarification regarding the appointment of Library faculty and will proceed with the appointments from among the broader university faculty.
He is still seeking candidates and is interested in making sure users of physical collections - not just digital collections - are represented.
In a related discussion, senate leadership has expressed concern about the use of search firms and their taking liberties with initial culls of candidates.
The search committees expect to participate fully at every step and this feels like an affront.
The Vice Provost has agreed to bring these concerns to the Provost and President. iv.

Copyright statement - the General Counsel’s office is still looking at this.
It obviously didn’t make the Vice Provost’s announcement for the start of the spring semester so the goal now is to have something finalized in time for a Fall 2026 announcement. v.
Commencement schedule - There will be eight events (two Friday, three each Saturday and Sunday).
FSEC members are encouraged to share the Grand Marshal role and Pres.
Williams would like to settle on a schedule soon so the event organizers can be informed and have correct information for contact and program purposes. vi.
URI at the Statehouse - the Senate will not have a booth or table at the March 26 event but will fully participate otherwise.
Staff was asked to procure some sort of button or pin that can be worn to the event as a representation of the Faculty Senate.
A bus will be available but FSEC members should feel free to drive. vii.
Other - Pres.
Williams met with Vice Provost Adams today and discussed, among other things, a change that is proposed in how faculty are awarded emeritus status.

The changes affect Chapter 7 of the University Manual and the proposal calls for insertion of language that would require faculty to have served ‘honorably and meritoriously’ during their years of service.
The same language would apply to Deans and other administrators who seek emeritus status.
Apparently the intention of the change is to allow the status to be bestowed on individuals who may not meet the 10-years-of-service minimum who might still qualify under the new provision.
FSEC members agreed some clarification is needed to specify some process for establishing ‘honorable and meritorious’ service 3

- including definitions or examples and an assignment of roles so it is clear who is making the determination. 6. Report of the Coordinator i. Effective Dates of Legislation - staff will create a process to help ensure all UM revisions have an ‘effective date’ as part of the bill going forward. ii. Student worker hiring update - two graduate students have been interviewed and a third is coming in next week. It looks like the senate office will get 10 - 15 hours of help per week. iii. Outreach re: Legislation - The senate has been busy with a lot of UM amendments this year and it doesn’t appear that adequate outreach is occurring as the office has spent a lot of time answering questions and making corrections to proposals that don’t comply with new protocols. It is hoped that one of the new graduate student workers can help with effective messaging but if FSEC members have thoughts on a strategy that can be implemented, they should feel free to share. It was agreed that if the college liaisons are effectively launched, this situation could improve but thought will be given to more near-term actions. 7. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. A question was raised about the senate’s budget, but no details are yet available regarding what the Provost plans to program for next year. 8.
